meta.review_notes: Strict legal-safe re-analysis. Camera & Microphone, Children's Data Handling, and Health & Biometric Data marked as unknown due to silence in policy. Behavioral & Ad Tracking downgraded to safe because policy explicitly states Dropbox does not sell data to advertisers and cookies are used for service functionality and self-promotion only. Score: 82 (Grade A).

app.name: Dropbox
app.description: A cloud storage and file synchronization service that lets you store, share, and access your files from anywhere.

verdict.one_liner: Dropbox states it does not sell your data to advertisers and gives you solid controls to access and delete your data.
verdict.summary: Dropbox collects account information, stored files, contacts, usage activity, and device identifiers. The company explicitly states it will not sell data to advertisers or other third parties. It shares information with trusted third parties for support, corporate affiliates, and collaborators. Third-party apps connected via APIs exchange data under their own terms. Users can access, amend, download, and delete personal data through account settings. After account deletion, Dropbox initiates deletion after 30 days, though residual copies may persist on backups or longer where legal obligations demand.
verdict.recommendation_reason: Dropbox has strong privacy practices with no ad tracking, no data selling, and good user controls for data deletion and export.

red.title: Shares data with third parties
red.plain_english: Dropbox states it shares your data with trusted third-party companies that help run the service, like customer support providers, and with other Dropbox Companies.

red.title: Collects device identifiers
red.plain_english: Dropbox states it collects device identifiers to recognize your devices and maintain security.

green.title: No ads or ad tracking
green.plain_english: Dropbox explicitly states: 'We won't sell it to advertisers or other third parties.' It does not use your data to show you targeted ads from outside advertisers.

green.title: Strong user data controls
green.plain_english: Dropbox states you can access, amend, download, and delete your personal data through your account settings.

green.title: Account deletion available
green.plain_english: Dropbox states you can delete your account and it will initiate deletion after 30 days, though some copies may remain on backups longer.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state whether the app accesses your camera or microphone.
categories.detail: No camera or microphone access mentioned in the reviewed privacy policy.

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states your devices may transmit location information to the Services depending on their settings. It uses this to detect abuse and troubleshoot bugs.
categories.detail: Location information may be transmitted by devices depending on settings. Used for abuse detection and bug troubleshooting. Not explicitly described as GPS.
categories.policy_excerpt: Your devices (depending on their settings) may also transmit location information to the Services. For example, we use device information to detect abuse and identify and troubleshoot bugs.
concerns: Location transmitted depending on device settings

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states you may choose to give it access to your contacts to make sharing and collaboration easier. If you do, it will store those contacts on its servers.
categories.detail: Contacts accessed for sharing files with others. Uploaded to servers if user opts in.
categories.policy_excerpt: You may choose to give us access to your contacts to make it easy for you, and your Dropbox Team if you're a Dropbox Team user, to do things like share and collaborate on Your Stuff, send messages, and invite others to use the Services. If you do, we'll store those contacts on our servers.
concerns: Contacts uploaded to servers for sharing

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: Dropbox needs access to your files so it can store and sync them. This is the main purpose of the app.
categories.detail: Full file access is required for cloud storage and syncing. Files are stored, processed, and transmitted by Dropbox as part of the core service.
categories.policy_excerpt: Our Services are designed as a simple and personalized way for you to store your files, documents, photos, comments, messages, data from connected services, and so on ('Your Stuff')... we store, process, and transmit Your Stuff as well as information related to it.

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it shares some data with trusted companies that help provide the service, with other Dropbox Companies, and with collaborators you choose to work with. It explicitly says it will not sell your data to advertisers.
categories.detail: Shared with trusted third parties for support, corporate affiliates, and collaborators. Third-party apps connected via APIs exchange data under their own terms. Team admins may access team account data. Legal disclosures may occur for law enforcement or public interest.
categories.policy_excerpt: We may share information as discussed below, but we won't sell it to advertisers or other third parties.
concerns: API-connected apps have their own data rules
Team admins may access team accounts

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it collects your name, email, phone number, payment info, and physical address when you sign up or upgrade.
categories.detail: Account information like name, email, phone number, payment info, and physical address collected for account management.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect, and associate with your account, the information you provide to us when you do things such as sign up for your account, upgrade to a paid plan, and set up two-factor authentication (like your name, email address, phone number, payment info, and physical address).

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it does not sell your data to advertisers. It uses cookies and pixel tags for service functionality and to promote its own services, not for third-party behavioral ad tracking.
categories.detail: Cookies and pixel tags are used for service functionality, understanding interactions, and promoting Dropbox services. Marketing is opt-out. Third-party service providers may set cookies to promote Dropbox services. No third-party ad targeting is described.
categories.policy_excerpt: We won't sell it to advertisers or other third parties.

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state how Dropbox handles children's data.
categories.detail: No specific children's data handling information found in the reviewed privacy policy.

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it logs your usage activity and IP address to keep the service running and secure.
categories.detail: Usage activity logged for service functionality and security. IP addresses collected from devices used to access the service.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect information related to how you use the Services, including actions you take in your account (like sharing, editing, viewing, creating and moving files or folders, and sending and receiving electronic signature requests and other transactions).

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it collects device identifiers, IP addresses, browser type, and device type to recognize your devices and keep your account secure.
categories.detail: Device identifiers collected for security and service functionality. Includes IP address, browser type, device type, and identifiers associated with devices.
categories.policy_excerpt: We also collect information from and about the devices you use to access the Services. This includes things like IP addresses, the type of browser and device you use, the web page you visited before coming to our sites, and identifiers associated with your devices.

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state whether Dropbox collects health or biometric data.
categories.detail: No health or biometric data collection mentioned in the reviewed privacy policy.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it collects payment info when you upgrade to a paid plan. Actual card processing is handled by third parties.
categories.detail: Payment information collected for paid plans. Third-party processors handle actual transactions.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect, and associate with your account, the information you provide to us when you do things such as sign up for your account, upgrade to a paid plan... (like your name, email address, phone number, payment info, and physical address).

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states you can delete your account and your data, but it takes 30 days and some copies might stay on backups longer or be retained for legal obligations.
categories.detail: Users may access, amend, download, and delete personal data through account settings. Following account deletion, Dropbox initiates deletion after 30 days, though residual copies may persist briefly on backups or longer where legal obligations demand.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you delete your account, we'll initiate deletion of this information after 30 days. But please note: (1) there might be some latency in deleting this information from our servers and back-up storage; and (2) we may retain this information if necessary to comply with our legal obligations, resolve disputes, or enforce our agreements.

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: Dropbox states it will notify you if a revision meaningfully reduces your rights.
categories.detail: Dropbox states it may revise the privacy policy from time to time and will post the most current version. It explicitly says: 'If a revision meaningfully reduces your rights, we will notify you.'
categories.policy_excerpt: We may revise this Privacy Policy from time to time, and will post the most current version on our website. If a revision meaningfully reduces your rights, we will notify you.
